title: Register a short-term rental (homestay): zoning permit or registry, business license and lodging tax
question: I want to rent out my home or a room for short stays in Albemarle County. What permit or registration do I need, and what taxes apply?
office: Community Development Department, Zoning Division (Zoning Administrator): homestay zoning clearance, special exceptions and the Short-Term Rental Registry; Department of Finance & Budget, Office of Revenue Administration (Business & Personal Tax Unit): business license, transient occupancy tax, attestation and business personal property
summary: Albemarle calls rentals of under 30 days homestays. They are allowed only at an owner's full-time home (an owner lives on the parcel 180 days a year) in a detached single-family house, not a townhouse, duplex, apartment or condo. Before renting, get a Homestay Zoning Clearance from Community Development in Civic Access ($120 plus 4% on the fee schedule; the Homestays page says $169 plus 4%), pass a fire and building inspection, notify neighbors, and join the Short-Term Rental Registry (free at first). Then get a County business license, file the annual attestation by March 1, and pay the 9% lodging tax monthly by the 20th on direct bookings. Each year, renew the registry and pass a $50 fire inspection.

legal_basis.quote: "Short-term rental" means the provision of a room or space that is suitable or intended for occupancy for dwelling, sleeping, or lodging purposes, for a period of fewer than 30 consecutive days, in exchange for a charge for the occupancy.
any locality may, by ordinance, establish a short-term rental registry and require operators within the locality to register annually.
The registration shall be ministerial in nature
A locality may charge a reasonable fee for such registration related to the actual costs of establishing and maintaining the registry.
No ordinance shall require a person to register pursuant to this section if such person is (i) licensed by the Real Estate Board or is a property owner who is represented by a real estate licensee
such ordinance may include a penalty not to exceed $500 per violation for an operator required to register who offers for short-term rental a property that is not registered with the locality.

No local ordinance shall prohibit an operator from offering a property as a short-term rental solely on the basis that such operator is a lessee or sublessee, provided that the property owner has granted permission for such property's use as a short-term rental.

No local ordinance enacted after December 31, 2023, or any subsequent amendment, shall require that a special exception, special use, or conditional use permit be obtained for the use of a residential dwelling as a short-term rental where the dwelling unit is also legally occupied by the property owner as his primary residence.
nothing herein shall be construed to prohibit, limit, or otherwise supersede existing local authority to regulate the short-term rental of property through general land use and zoning authority.
notwithstanding any other provisions of this article, the governing body of any locality may reserve unto itself the right to issue such special exceptions.

steps.step: Check that your home can be a homestay
steps.who: Owner who lives on the parcel
steps.how: A homestay is any rental of part or all of a home for less than 30 days at a time, including Airbnb, VRBO and similar listings. It must be accessory to the owner's full-time home: at least one owner must live on the parcel 180 days or more each calendar year. Vacation homes do not qualify. Homestays are allowed only in detached single-family houses (or their accessory apartment), not in townhouses, duplexes, apartments or condominiums. Rentals of 30 days or more are not homestays and need no clearance, though a business license may be needed. Check your address in the County GIS, because some "Charlottesville" mailing addresses are in Albemarle County and others in the City, which has its own rules. Private covenants and HOA or condominium rules may also limit rentals.

steps.step: Work out the limits that apply to your parcel
steps.how: Look up your zoning district and acreage in the County GIS. In the Residential and Planned Development districts, and on Rural Areas parcels under 5 acres: one homestay per parcel, at most 2 guest bedrooms, only in the house or its accessory apartment, and an owner (or approved resident manager) must stay overnight on the parcel during every rental. On Rural Areas parcels of 5 acres or more: up to 5 guest bedrooms, up to two homestays if the parcel has two houses, accessory structures built on or before August 7, 2019 may be used, and, if the homestay is approved for "unhosted" stays, the owner may be away for up to 7 rental days a month and 45 a year (keep a log). On those parcels, each house with a homestay must meet the permitted density, must have and use a development right if the parcel is under 21 acres, and may have only one homestay. Everywhere: on-site parking of 1 space per guest bedroom plus 2 for the house, no street parking, primary-structure setbacks (in the Rural Areas the County table adds screening; on parcels of 5 acres or more the ordinance requires it for homestay structures and parking within 125 feet of a neighbor's lot), no restaurant and no events with people who are not staying there.
steps.quote: A maximum of two guest rooms used for sleeping may be permitted with each homestay use, provided that by special exception, the Board of Supervisors may authorize the homestay use of up to five guest rooms.

steps.step: If you need a waiver, apply for a special exception from the Board of Supervisors
steps.who: Owner; Community Development (Zoning) reviews; the Board of Supervisors decides
steps.how: Only the rules the ordinance marks as waivable can be changed: up to 5 guest bedrooms (instead of 2) or use of an accessory structure on smaller or residential parcels, reduced setbacks, accessory structures built after August 7, 2019 in the Rural Areas, and a resident manager in place of owner residency. Talk to Zoning staff before applying. Apply in Civic Access (Special Exception application). The Board decides at a public meeting after notice to the owners of abutting parcels. The fee is not refunded if the request is denied.
steps.deadline: Before you rent in a way that needs the waiver
steps.fee: $980 plus the 4% technology surcharge (not refundable if denied); $1,125 plus 4% from January 1, 2027 under Ordinance No. 26-1(1)

steps.step: Gather what the clearance application needs
steps.how: Prepare: the responsible agent's contact information (the agent can be you, but must be within 30 miles whenever guests are there); a floor plan sketch showing every structure used for the homestay, owner-occupied bedrooms, guest bedrooms and spaces, the entrance, on-site parking, outdoor lighting and signage, and setbacks; the planned number of guest rooms and outdoor lighting details; and two documents proving you live there permanently (such as a driver's license or voter registration card), which you must show in person during review. Both the owner and the responsible agent sign. If the property has a well, the Virginia Department of Health strongly recommends a coliform test.
steps.quote: The owner must provide two forms of verification of permanent residency, such as a driver's license, voter registration card, or other document(s) that the Zoning Administrator determines provide equivalent proof of permanent residence at the subject parcel(s).

steps.step: Apply for the Homestay Zoning Clearance in Civic Access and pay the fee
steps.who: Owner, applying to the Community Development Department (Zoning)
steps.how: Register an account in the County's Civic Access portal, then open the Homestay Clearance application, upload the documents and pay the fee. You can track the application and staff comments in Civic Access. If you need help, contact Community Development at 434-296-5832 or cddinquiry@albemarle.org, or visit the North Wing at 401 McIntire Road.
steps.deadline: Before the first rental (the clearance must be obtained prior to conducting a homestay)
steps.fee: $120 plus the 4% technology surcharge on the County fee schedule; the Homestays page instead states $169 plus 4% as the "application and inspection fee" (see fees and caveats); the fee schedule amount becomes $140 plus 4% from January 1, 2027 under Ordinance No. 26-1(1)
steps.quote: A parcel owner must obtain a zoning clearance under section 31.5 prior to conducting a homestay.

steps.step: Enroll on the Short-Term Rental Registry at the same time
steps.how: Give the operator's name and home address, the rental address, guest bedrooms, and the responsible agent's details. The Homestays page says to email the completed Short-Term Rental Registry form to homestays@albemarle.org; the Homestay Clearances page also offers a Short-Term Rental Registry Enrollment Form in Civic Access. State law exempts real estate licensees and owners represented by one, registered time-shares, lodging licensed by the Virginia Department of Health, and businesses licensed by the County for renting or managing real property (County Code § 7-602(C) follows it).
steps.deadline: With the clearance application (the registry form says before opening for business); then every year
steps.fee: No fee for the first enrollment

steps.step: Install the required safety items within 30 days of applying
steps.how: Post the address at the driveway (and on each structure if there are more than two; each homestay structure needs its own address). Mount a 2A:10BC fire extinguisher in the kitchen. Display an emergency evacuation floor plan with exits and the 911 address in each habitable room. Make sure every bedroom has an operable emergency escape window. No extension cords in place of permanent wiring (properly sized power strips with overcurrent protection are allowed). Keep the electrical panel accessible to guests. Install interconnected smoke alarms in and outside each sleeping room and on every story, as the Building Code requires.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days of submitting the application

steps.step: Send the neighbor notice and give a copy to Community Development
steps.who: Owner; County staff supply the list of abutting owners
steps.how: After the application is received, staff give you the list of owners of adjoining parcels. Mail each a letter saying you are applying for a Homestay Zoning Clearance, with your name, phone number and emergency contact, and the responsible agent's name, phone number and emergency number. Send a copy of the letter to Albemarle County Community Development, 401 McIntire Road, Charlottesville, VA 22902. The ordinance also requires updated contact information every year after approval; it does not say clearly whether that goes to Zoning, to the neighbors or to both, so ask Zoning.
steps.deadline: Before the clearance is approved; updated contact information annually after that

steps.step: Pass the fire and building safety inspection, and get any Health Department approval
steps.who: Building official and fire official (Community Development and Fire Rescue); Virginia Department of Health
steps.how: Schedule the inspection through Community Development once the safety items are in place. The first inspection is covered by the clearance fee; failing it can mean paying for more inspections. The ordinance requires approval of the use by the building official, the fire official and the Virginia Department of Health before the clearance is approved. The County's Homestays page says Health Department transient lodging review is needed if you will serve food to guests.
steps.fee: First inspection included in the clearance fee; re-inspections may cost extra

steps.step: Zoning reviews and issues the Homestay Zoning Clearance
steps.how: Staff check the application, the neighbor notice, the inspections and residency. The County says approval usually takes 3 to 4 weeks but does not guarantee it. State law requires the Zoning Administrator to respond to a request for a zoning decision within 90 days unless you agree to longer. A denial, or a condition you disagree with, can be appealed to the Board of Zoning Appeals within 30 days (see escalation).
steps.deadline: Usually 3 to 4 weeks (not guaranteed); 90 days under Va. Code § 15.2-2286(A)(4)

steps.step: Get a County business license from the Department of Finance & Budget
steps.who: Operator; Office of Revenue Administration, Business & Personal Tax Unit (the Director of Finance holds the commissioner of the revenue's powers)
steps.how: Fill in the New Business License Application. In Step 7, tick "Rent Rooms for <30 days" and give actual or estimated gross receipts; the form asks for proof of zoning approval but does not require it before you apply. Email it to tax@albemarle.org, mail it to County of Albemarle, 401 McIntire Rd, Suite 133, Charlottesville, VA 22902, or fax it to 434-243-7906. A new business cannot open an account online. For a new homestay the County says to apply after the clearance is approved; an existing unpermitted homestay gets the license first (step s18). The 2026 application says a $50 fee, or the tax when receipts are $100,000 or more, is due when you apply.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days of beginning business, to avoid the 10% late filing penalty (state law: before beginning business)
steps.fee: No fee if gross receipts are $25,000 or less; $50 if over $25,000 and under $100,000; at $100,000 or more, a tax at the rate the Homestays page gives as 0.0036 (36 cents per $100)

steps.step: File the Accommodations Provider Annual Attestation
steps.how: If every booking will go through a platform such as Airbnb, VRBO or Expedia (an accommodations intermediary), complete Sections 1 and 2: you then do not file monthly transient occupancy tax returns for the 12 months covered. If you take any direct bookings, complete Sections 1 and 3 and file monthly (step s13). List every property address and every platform you advertise on. File it with the business license application and then with each year's renewal, by email, mail, drop-off at the McIntire Road building or its payment boxes, fax, or the County's digital form.
steps.deadline: Each year by March 1 (or the first business day after, if March 1 is a weekend or holiday), with the business license renewal

steps.step: Collect and pay the 9% transient occupancy (lodging) tax on direct bookings every month
steps.who: Operator for bookings it takes directly; the platform (accommodations intermediary) for bookings it facilitates
steps.how: For stays under 30 consecutive days that you book yourself, add the 9% tax to the guest's bill and state it separately. File and pay each month for the previous month, online in the County business tax portal or on the County's Transient Occupancy Tax coupon (mail to the Business & Personal Tax Unit, 401 McIntire Road, Suite 133). File a separate return for each location, and file even when there were no sales. On the coupon, line 1 is total gross rentals and line 2 the rentals for which a platform collected the tax; attach the platform's statement. If you file online instead, the County says to report gross receipts not including the sales a platform facilitated. You may keep a 3% seller discount if you file and pay on time with no balance owed; platforms cannot. The tax collected is held in trust for the County.
steps.deadline: By the 20th of the month after the month the tax was collected (filings online by 11:59 PM ET on the due date)
steps.fee: 9% of taxable receipts, less a 3% seller discount when filed and paid on time

steps.step: Account for Virginia sales tax on direct bookings
steps.who: Operator for direct bookings; platforms for the bookings they facilitate
steps.how: Lodging is also subject to Virginia retail sales and use tax, which the County says is 5.3%. For bookings you take directly, you collect it and pay it to the Virginia Department of Taxation, which means registering with the Department as a dealer (a state process not modeled here). Platforms collect it on the bookings they handle. If you serve food or drinks, the County Food and Beverage tax also applies.

steps.step: File the business tangible personal property return for the furnishings
steps.how: Homestays are businesses for local tax purposes. Each year, report the furniture, decorations, appliances and other property used for the rental, as held on January 1, by year acquired and at full original cost, online or on the County return. The County page (June 2026 copy) gives a rate of $4.28 per $100 of assessed value, and the Board's calendar year 2026 tax rate resolution (April 22, 2026) kept $4.28; bills are due June 25 and December 5. Details are in the separate process business_tangible_personal_property_return.
steps.fee: $4.28 per $100 of assessed value (County page, June 2026; calendar year 2026 rate resolution of April 22, 2026)

steps.step: Run the homestay within the rules
steps.how: The responsible agent must be within 30 miles whenever guests are there, respond to any complaint and try in good faith to resolve it within 60 minutes, and may have to go to the property. Guests park on site, not on the street. Parties, events or weddings may include only the people staying there. If you are approved for unhosted stays, keep a log of each rental day you are away and give it to the Zoning Administrator within five business days if asked. Offering a property for short-term rental while it is not on the registry can bring a $500 penalty for each day it is offered, and it may not be offered again until the penalty is paid and the property registered; repeated registry violations, or more than three violations of state or County rules on the rental, can bar the property from short-term rental.
steps.quote: The responsible agent must respond and attempt in good faith to resolve any complaint(s) within 60 minutes of being contacted.

steps.who: Operator; Zoning staff (who send a reminder); Fire Marshal's office; Department of Finance & Budget
steps.how: On each anniversary of approval: renew the registry enrollment with an updated Short-Term Rental Registry Annual Application, and pass the annual fire safety inspection (call the Fire Marshal's office at 434-296-5833 to schedule). Provide updated contact information for you and the responsible agent each year (the ordinance's annual notice; ask Zoning whether it goes to Zoning, the neighbors or both). By March 1: renew the business license (online, by digital form or on paper; for the first 3 years on the full application) and file the accommodations attestation. Keep filing the lodging tax monthly if you take direct bookings, and the property return by May 1.
steps.deadline: Registry and fire inspection: each year by the anniversary of approval; business license and attestation: March 1
steps.fee: Registry re-enrollment $27 (Homestays page and County Code § 7-602(B)) or $30 (County fee schedule; $35 from January 1, 2027 under Ordinance No. 26-1(1)); annual fire safety inspection $50; business license fee as in s11

steps.step: Already renting without approval? Get the license and pay back taxes first
steps.who: Operator; Department of Finance & Budget; Community Development
steps.how: Contact the Business & Personal Tax Unit right away, get a business license, and pay the transient occupancy, sales, food and beverage and other taxes (with interest) for past rentals: you are liable for all of them since you started. Then contact Zoning and follow the clearance steps above. If the home cannot meet the homestay rules, stop renting, take down the listings, and tell Finance and Zoning you are closing.

steps.step: Close the accounts if you stop hosting
steps.who: Operator; Business & Personal Tax Unit; Zoning
steps.how: Tell the Business & Personal Tax Unit by email or letter (or tick the closure box on the renewal), and tell Zoning so the registry entry and inspections stop. Business personal property is not prorated: if you close after January 1 you are still billed for that year.

escalation.trigger: Homestay Zoning Clearance denied, or approved with a condition you dispute
escalation.next: Board of Zoning Appeals: file a notice of appeal giving the grounds with the Zoning Administrator and the Board; the County takes appeals through the "Appeal of Zoning Administrator's Determination" application in Civic Access ($350 plus 4%; $405 plus 4% from January 1, 2027)
escalation.quote: The appeal shall be taken within 30 days after the decision appealed from by filing with the zoning administrator, and with the board, a notice of appeal specifying the grounds thereof.

escalation.next: Zoning Administrator (Community Development): ask in writing for a decision; a written decision then starts the 30-day appeal period to the Board of Zoning Appeals
escalation.deadline: The Zoning Administrator must respond within 90 days of the request unless you agreed to a longer period
escalation.quote: The zoning administrator shall respond within 90 days of a request for a decision or determination on zoning matters within the scope of his authority unless the requester has agreed to a longer period.

escalation.trigger: Written notice of a zoning violation or order (for example, renting without a clearance, too many unhosted days, or street parking)
escalation.next: Board of Zoning Appeals (the appeal stays enforcement unless the Zoning Administrator certifies imminent peril)
escalation.deadline: Within 30 days of the notice, which must state the appeal right and fee; a 10-day period can apply to some short-term recurring violations; otherwise the notice becomes final and unappealable
escalation.quote: the decision shall be final and unappealable if not appealed within 30 days

escalation.trigger: Refused only because you rent the home (tenant or subtenant with the owner's permission)
escalation.next: Ask Zoning to apply state law; if refused in writing, appeal to the Board of Zoning Appeals; a claim that the ordinance conflicts with state law may in the end need a court
escalation.deadline: Within 30 days after a written refusal
escalation.quote: No local ordinance shall prohibit an operator from offering a property as a short-term rental solely on the basis that such operator is a lessee or sublessee, provided that the property owner has granted permission for such property's use as a short-term rental.

escalation.trigger: Board of Zoning Appeals decides against you (it must decide within 90 days of the filing)
escalation.next: Albemarle Circuit Court: petition filed with the Clerk, then served on the necessary parties within 30 days of filing
escalation.deadline: Within 30 days after the Board's final decision (mandatory and jurisdictional)
escalation.quote: Such 30-day filing requirement shall be mandatory and jurisdictional.

escalation.trigger: Board of Supervisors denies (or grants with conditions you dispute) a homestay special exception
escalation.next: Albemarle Circuit Court (the court for the county where the land is)
escalation.deadline: Within 30 days of the Board's decision (mandatory and jurisdictional)
escalation.quote: Every action contesting a decision of the local governing body adopting or failing to adopt a proposed zoning ordinance or amendment thereto or granting or failing to grant a special exception shall be filed within 30 days of the decision with the circuit court having jurisdiction of the land affected by the decision.

escalation.trigger: Business license assessment or classification disputed (for example a higher tax, a denied refund, or an estimated assessment)
escalation.next: Director of Finance: written administrative appeal to the Revenue Administration - Assessments Unit, 401 McIntire Road, Room 133
escalation.deadline: Within one year from the last day of the tax year assessed, or one year from the appealable event, whichever is later
escalation.basis: Va. Code §§ 58.1-3703.1(A)(5)(b), 15.2-521(A); County Notice of Taxpayer Appeal Rights
escalation.quote: may file an administrative appeal of the assessment within one year from the last day of the tax year for which such assessment is made, or within one year from the date of the appealable event, whichever is later, with the commissioner of the revenue or other local assessing official.

escalation.trigger: Director of Finance's determination on the business license appeal is adverse
escalation.next: Tax Commissioner (Virginia Department of Taxation); serve a copy on the County assessing official
escalation.deadline: Within 90 days of the Director's final local determination
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 58.1-3703.1(A)(6)(a); County Notice of Taxpayer Appeal Rights
escalation.quote: may appeal such assessment or determination to the Tax Commissioner within 90 days of the date of the determination by the commissioner of the revenue or other assessing official.

escalation.trigger: Lodging tax assessment believed wrong (for example, tax a platform already paid was not credited)
escalation.next: Director of Finance (application for correction of the assessment)
escalation.deadline: Within three years from the last day of the tax year, or one year from the assessment, whichever is later
escalation.quote: apply to the commissioner of the revenue or such other official who made the assessment for a correction thereof.

escalation.trigger: Still aggrieved by a lodging tax or business license assessment, or choosing to go straight to court
escalation.next: Albemarle Circuit Court (application to correct the assessment; "Albemarle County" is the named party)
escalation.deadline: Within three years from the last day of the tax year, one year from the assessment, or one year from the Tax Commissioner's final determination, whichever is later
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 58.1-3984(A); County Notice of Taxpayer Appeal Rights
escalation.quote: apply for relief to the circuit court of the county or city wherein such assessment was made.

escalation.trigger: Late filing or late payment penalty charged although the lateness was not your fault
escalation.next: Department of Finance & Budget (ask for the penalty and interest to be removed)
escalation.quote: Penalty and interest for failure to file a return or to pay a tax shall not be imposed if such failure was not the fault of the taxpayer

caveats: Albemarle County's website (www.albemarle.org) refuses automated readers, so the county pages and PDFs cited here are Internet Archive copies: they show the pages as they were when copied. The registry form is from a July 2024 copy. The Internet Archive holds no newer copies of the Homestays, Homestay Clearance, fee schedule, Finance Homestay, lodging tax, existing businesses and business property pages. The live pages may have changed since; confirm on them before you act. The County's Terms and Conditions bar reposting its content without written permission, so the County's own words are not reprinted on this page; each step links the County page instead.

Local law sources. The County Code is published on Municode, whose terms forbid automated access, so it has not been checked. Ordinance text comes from the County's Legistar system (webapi.legistar.com). The Zoning Ordinance § 5.1.48 text is the County's own "Att. C - Homestay Ordinance" attached to a March 4, 2026 Board of Supervisors homestay item; its history note (Ord. 22-18(2), 4-6-22) shows the 2022 amendments were adopted. The registry (County Code §§ 7-601 to 7-604) is quoted from the 2020 Chapter 7 rewrite, whose history notes date each section to Ord. 19-7(1), 8-7-19, so the quoted words are the 2019 enacted text. The lodging tax (§§ 15-901, 15-902) and Fire Marshal fee quotes come from proposed ordinances in Board agenda packets; the Legistar event items for the hearings (August 7, 2019, April 24, 2024, September 17, 2025) record no vote. The 12/2025 tax coupon states the Board adopted the 9% rate effective July 1, 2024 (it says after a hearing in May 2024), and the attestation form applies Sec. 15-902 from January 1, 2026, so adoption of those is inferred from the County's own forms. Quotes use only text the drafts leave unchanged or newly add (struck text is left out).

Clearance fee conflict. The Community Development Fees page (August 2026 copy) lists "Zoning Clearance - Homestay" at $120, plus the 4% technology surcharge, and the March 2026 draft fee ordinance shows $120 as the current County Code § 1-504 amount. The Homestays page (March 2026 copy) says "$169 + 4%" as an "application and inspection fee". Whether $169 includes the first inspection or is an outdated figure was not found. Ask Community Development, or check the amount Civic Access charges.

Registry fee conflict. County Code § 7-602(B) (2019 text) and the Homestays page say $27 for each registration or re-enrollment. The fee schedule page lists "Short Term Rental Registry" at $30 (County Code § 1-505, Ord. 23-1(1) of December 6, 2023, which is later than the 2019 text), and the 2020 registry form's office box shows "$30" or "$0 with clearance application". The first enrollment is free per the Homestays page. The fee schedule applies its 4% technology surcharge to each fee on it, with exceptions that do not include the registry, but the Homestays page states the $27 without a surcharge; whether the surcharge is charged on the registry fee in practice, and whether it applies to the Fire Marshal's $50 inspection fee (which is on a separate schedule), was not stated.

Fee increases from January 1, 2027. Ordinance No. 26-1(1) amending the County fee schedule was deferred on April 15, 2026 and adopted on April 22, 2026 (Legistar 26-256, motion to adopt Attachment B passed), effective January 1, 2027. It raises the homestay clearance to $140, the registry to $35, a Board of Zoning Appeals appeal to $405 and a special exception to $1,125 (the 4% surcharge continues). The amounts were read from the adopted attachment's table, whose text extraction is column-shifted; the values match the March 2026 draft. The Homestays page also gives an outdated $508 special exception fee in one place; the fee schedule says $980.

How to enroll on the registry. The Homestays page (March 2026) says to email the registry form to homestays@albemarle.org; the Homestay Clearances page (April 2026) lists a "Short-Term Rental Registry Enrollment Form" in Civic Access. The PDF form is version 9.17.20 and still uses the older term "whole house rental" (now "unhosted stays"). Use the method Zoning staff direct.

Lodging tax rate. The Finance Transient Occupancy Tax page and the 12/2025 coupon give 9% (raised from 8% on July 1, 2024). The FAQ on the Community Development Homestays page still says 5% and gives a 60/40 tourism split; those figures are out of date and are not used here.

Platform bookings. Since January 1, 2026, a host whose bookings all go through platforms and who files the annual attestation need not file monthly returns (Va. Code § 58.1-3827(D); Finance Homestay page). The older Transient Occupancy Tax page and the coupon still say to file a coupon with the platform's statement even when the platform pays. A host who files the attestation should follow the attestation; a host with any direct bookings files monthly and reports platform receipts on line 2.

Health Department. Zoning Ordinance § 5.1.48(a)(4) requires Virginia Department of Health approval of the use before a clearance is approved. The Homestays page says Health Department transient lodging review is needed if you serve food. Which applies to a homestay that serves no food was not confirmed; ask Zoning. The County page lists a named Health Department staff contact, which was not recorded.

Tenants. The County ordinance is written around owner residency. Va. Code § 15.2-983(D) bars refusing an operator solely because the operator is a lessee or sublessee with the owner's permission. How Albemarle handles tenant-operators was not found on the pages read.

Special exceptions and the 2024 state law. Va. Code § 15.2-983(D) bars requiring a special exception for an owner-occupied primary residence only in ordinances enacted after December 31, 2023, or later amendments. Albemarle's § 5.1.48 was last amended April 6, 2022, per its history note, so its special exceptions still apply; a future amendment would be subject to the state limit.

Business license classification and timing. The Homestays page FAQ gives a rate of 0.0036 for $100,000 or more in receipts, matching the County's "Repair, Personal, Business, and Other Services" class; the County rate table also has a $0.20 per $100 class for renting houses and apartments. The Office of Revenue Administration sets the class. The County says to apply within 30 days of beginning business, while Va. Code § 58.1-3703.1(A)(2)(a) says to apply before beginning business; applying before the first booking is safest. Full license rules are in the separate process bpol_business_license.

Food and drink. Serving guests food requires Health Department approval and collecting the County food and beverage tax. That tax is modelled in the separate process meals_tax_filing and its rate was not checked here. The ordinance bars a restaurant as an accessory use.

State sales tax. The 5.3% rate is the County's statement for Albemarle and was not checked against Virginia Department of Taxation sources. Registering with the Department as a dealer is a state process not modeled here.

Appeal period for violations. Va. Code § 15.2-2286(A)(4) lets a zoning ordinance set a 10-day appeal period for some short-term, recurring violations, and the County's determinations page mentions a 10-day period for temporary or seasonal commercial uses. Whether any homestay violation carries the shorter period depends on the notice; act within 10 days to be safe. The County's own BZA appeal provisions (Zoning Ordinance § 34.3 and related sections) and any civil penalty schedule for zoning violations were not read.

Registry penalties. County Code § 7-604 makes Community Development responsible for imposing registry penalties, but no appeal route for a registry penalty or a refused registration was found in the Chapter 7 text read. Because the registry is in Chapter 7 rather than the Zoning Ordinance, it is not clear that the Board of Zoning Appeals route applies; ask Community Development, or consult a lawyer about a court challenge. The registration itself is ministerial under Va. Code § 15.2-983(B)(1). Va. Code § 15.2-983(B)(2)(iv) also exempts operators licensed or registered with the locality for the rental or management of real property; the County's pages require every homestay to enroll, and whether a homestay's own County business license falls within that exemption was not addressed by the County.

Timelines. The 3 to 4 week approval estimate, the 30-day safety installation deadline and the neighbor-letter process come from a homestay guide dated March 28, 2023, still linked from the Homestay Clearances page in 2026. The Homestay Hotline number is from the same guide and may be out of date.

Not observed. The Civic Access application screens (the County says you must register first), the County's digital attestation form and the online business tax portal were not opened, and nothing was submitted. The BTPP return PDF was not opened; see business_tangible_personal_property_return.
Versions. The index marks Va. Code § 15.2-2286 as effective until January 1, 2027 and holds no successor text; re-check it after that date.

Privacy. The County pages name planners, inspectors and compliance staff with personal mailboxes and extensions; none are recorded. Only office lines, the cddinquiry@, homestays@ and tax@ office mailboxes, the Fire Marshal's office line and official portals are listed.
Private rules. Va. Code § 15.2-983(E) keeps recorded covenants, condominium instruments and property owners' association declarations in force; they may bar or limit rentals the County allows.

Site terms. The albemarle.org Terms and Conditions allow browsing for informational purposes but say no one may reuse or repost the site's content without written permission, so the County's own words are not reprinted on this page; each entry links the County page instead.
